title: Prove a strict column-defect bound for mixed-cycle matrices
body:
**Scoped negative theorem:** if q>=5 is prime, b>=1 and an n-by-m matrix over roots of order 3q^b has orthogonal columns, with n=q+3 and d=n-m, then `m^2 < d^2(4d-3)`. Thus eight rows permit at most five columns, and 104 rows permit at most ninety. These are necessary upper bounds; attainment is not claimed. **No new kappa** follows.

Read the [proof](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/fefebaf8285f3c46f75a815657acbf48780763fb/research/mixed-cycle-column-defect/PROOF.md), [exact checks and bound table](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/fefebaf8285f3c46f75a815657acbf48780763fb/research/mixed-cycle-column-defect/RESULT.json), [checker](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/fefebaf8285f3c46f75a815657acbf48780763fb/research/mixed-cycle-column-defect/verify.py), [source pins](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/fefebaf8285f3c46f75a815657acbf48780763fb/research/mixed-cycle-column-defect/SOURCE-PINS.json) and [credits](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/fefebaf8285f3c46f75a815657acbf48780763fb/research/mixed-cycle-column-defect/CREDITS.md). This extends [PR #7762](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/7762) from one missing column to an arbitrary column defect.

The projected star gives a Hermitian q-power-root block K and a d-row remainder R with `K^2-3K-qI=-R*R`. The quadratic is irreducible over the q-power cyclotomic field, so its two root multiplicities agree. Trace, squared trace and the rank of R give the non-strict inequality. Equality would make the rows of R orthogonal, which forces q to divide m and then q=9. This contradiction makes the bound strict. In particular, q=101,m=91 satisfies the non-strict spectral relaxation but cannot occur.

Python 3.12 and the standard library:

```sh
python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/mixed-cycle-column-defect
```

Both registered modes print:

```text
PASS_MIXED_CYCLE_COLUMN_DEFECT
Strict bound m^2 < d^2(4d-3), d=q+3-m: written proof
36 exact block fixtures; 125 polynomial grid points; 24 prime bounds
Eight rows permit at most five columns; 104 rows permit at most ninety
Equality obstruction, positive controls, fault controls and unchanged source replay pass
```

Checks cover 2,828 exact block entries and all 11,193 multiplicity cases for primes 5 through 101. Three polynomial identities are verified on a grid that determines all coefficients. Valid two-column controls, a deleted-root control and four changed block formulas distinguish the hypotheses. Synthetic block fixtures check an identity; they are not asserted to be orthogonal matrices. The general theorem is the written proof, with classical cycle and quadratic-subfield inputs.

All sixteen retained source files are authenticated. The unchanged PR7762 and nested PR7744 verifiers pass, as do normal/optimized registered replay, syntax/indentation, committed bytes/source history/modes, export and sealed read-only Git-free serial replay. Hosted CI did not certify this package. The [plan job](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/44441318486/job/135282566921) failed in the shared `test_current_ci_section_matches_selected_record`: the base guide names frontier6030 while the selected record requires `make frontier7000-verify`. The log reports 760 tests, one failure and 24 skipped; package replay was skipped. This package changes no shared CI file. Local replay remains the scientific evidence.

Ali Romman (@aliromman) supplied the [projected-star proof](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/d33fe8562c86888307cbba4a2aa92490212c8d78/research/mixed-cycle-column-obstruction/PROOF.md) and [source checker](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/d33fe8562c86888307cbba4a2aa92490212c8d78/research/mixed-cycle-column-obstruction/verify.py). Nick Petalas (@petalas) supplied the two-prime projection and released question in [PR #7744](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/7744), with its pinned [proof](https://github.com/petalas/integer-mult-bounds/blob/7dc85513e8ee9b771a5856f027cf199936f85af0/research/two-prime-column-completion/README.md) and [prime-power arithmetic](https://github.com/petalas/integer-mult-bounds/blob/7dc85513e8ee9b771a5856f027cf199936f85af0/research/two-prime-column-completion/verify.py). All predecessor notices remain intact. Classical inputs are [Lam–Leung Theorem 3.3 and Corollary 3.4](https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/9511209#page=7) and [Sharifi Lemma 3.2.2](https://www.math.ucla.edu/~sharifi/notes/algnum-ch03.html).

Sharp attainable column counts, other row counts, larger powers of three, more prime factors, approximate orthogonality, physical preparation and complete caller pricing remain open. The selected cold replay, Lean and Docker were not run. All five framework assumptions and the selected frontier remain unchanged. No independent human/formal-kernel acceptance or global literature priority is claimed.
